There are two main limitations of this analysis, the first being that this is a surface measurement and therefore it may not be representative of any preferred orientation within the thickness of the film. The second limitation is that the method requires excellent visualization of the crystals on the surface of the films, and there were a limited number of images available for this analysis. However, the potential for alignment of crystallites may be important for the films 19 DE-EE0009099 to function as electrocaloric materials, as the alignment of crystallites may help lower the energy barrier for dipole orientation33,34 and lead to the improvement of electrocaloric properties. Electrospray processing, a thin film fabrication method, was used for the first time to successfully generate EC thin film materials. Results demonstrated that ES processing can be used to fabricate terpolymer thin films with a more consistent thickness, uniform, and smoother surface than solution-casted films. ES films a higher crystallinity compared with the SC films and applying a higher annealing temperature can further enhance the crystallinity of the thin film, giving the opportunity to raise the entropy change in the terpolymer thin film. When films are annealed at 60˚C, SC films appear to have a greater ability to store and recover electrical energy due to the smaller crystallite size compared to the ES film. However, when the films are annealed at 120˚C, ES film displayed larger dielectric responses and lower energy loss compared to the SC film. It was also observed that the ES film annealed at 120˚C may also result in a more-ordered crystallite and the alignment of crystallite may contribute to the enhancement of dielectric constant, although more experiments are needed to determine if this alignment persists through the thickness of the film. The EC temperature lifted for ES A120 using an IR camera showed a ∆T was 3.6˚C and ECE the EC strength ∆T /E of this film was 0.036˚C MV m-1 measured at 100 MV m-1 at room ECE temperature. These results appear to be similar to, or potentially exceeding, the existing literature values for thin film electrocalorics measured at or near room temperature, which is an exciting finding for a new fabrication method in this application space. While films prepared by ES processing required less time to manufacture than solution casting in this work, it is noted that advanced solution casting techniques were not employed. When considering manufacturability, both electrospray processing and solution casting are more scalable than spin coating, but electrospray processing can generate thinner films than solution casting and spin coating. This study encourages further development of electrospray processing as a new method of fabricating EC material thin films with high quality, which we envision to have the potential to meet manufacturing demands in the practical application in the future.
